about_page.label: About CDCat
about_page.title: A {em} built for music lovers like you
about_page.lead: CDCat is a {nonprofit} music database founded by a group of {lovers}, with a focus on lesser-known {doujin} and {japanese}.

highlights.archive_desc: CDCat preserves music metadata that might otherwise disappear. This matters especially for independent and doujin releases whose circles and official sites may no longer exist.
highlights.timeline_desc: Record what you have heard and loved, build a lasting listening history, and share the artists and songs that matter to you.
highlights.creator_desc: Document standard, limited, made-to-order, hi-res, and download editions alongside store bonuses and official sales links, so listeners can understand and support each release.
highlights.developer_desc: CDCat will provide a public API and documentation. Build lyric tools, cover matching, or your own applications on top of community-maintained data.
highlights.relations_desc: Connect music to games, anime, films, television, entries, and series so it can be explored from multiple perspectives.
highlights.community_desc: Beyond music metadata, CDCat aims to welcome discussion of audio gear, physical media, digital releases, production techniques, and creative work.
highlights.stories_desc: Future features will connect interviews, booklet material, and contributed lyrics to help listeners understand how music is made.

about_page.join_desc: Albums, artists and entries are open for you to add or correct, and contributors review every submission.
about_page.guides_desc: Start here if you would like to help edit the database.
about_page.guide_basics_desc: What albums, artists, events, entries and the rest are, and how they connect.
about_page.guide_research_desc: What to look for before contributing metadata.
about_page.guide_submit_desc: How to use the editor, from adding an album to correcting one, and what every option means.
about_page.docs_desc: CDCat's website frontend is open source on GitHub. If you can code, come help make it better.
about_page.api_docs_desc: Lets other sites and apps read CDCat's music data, for lyric tools, cover matching and more.
about_page.frontend_repo_desc: Bug fixes, design improvements and new features are all welcome as issues or pull requests.
about_page.recruit_desc: Translation, proofreading, art, cataloguing… plenty to do without writing code.
about_page.community_desc: No coding needed: share your ideas or report problems in the discussions or our groups.
about_page.discussions_desc: Report issues and talk about new features
about_page.legal_desc: The rules for using CDCat, and how we handle your information.
about_page.terms_desc: The rules of use, content licensing and moderation.
about_page.privacy_desc: What we collect, how we use it and your rights.

home.seo_title: CDCat — Japanese Music Database for Doujin, Vocaloid, Anime and Games
home.seo_description: Explore Japanese music, doujin releases, Vocaloid, anime and game soundtracks, events, and detailed track credits on CDCat.
home.seo_keywords: Japanese music,doujin music,Vocaloid,Touhou Project,anime soundtrack,game music,music database,track credits

hero.title:
Serious listeners deserve
serious liner notes.
hero.body: CDCat catalogs albums, tracks and credits from doujin, anime, game and VOCALOID music, sorted and checked bit by bit by its community.
hero.figure: Exploded view of a portable CD player: top lid, disc, optical pickup, chassis, main board and bottom shell

album.title:
Down to every disc
and every track.
album.body: Track lists and lengths, who composed, arranged and wrote each song, catalog numbers and prices, first-press and shop bonuses, and the event where it came out. Whatever is worth noting about an album has a place here.
album.figure: Exploded view of a Japanese CD release: front cover, booklet, disc, tray, inlay, obi strip and case

listen.title:
What you've heard,
what you want.
listen.body: Mark albums as plan to listen, wishlist, completed or owned, give them a score and a few words, and keep the ones you love as favorites.
listen.figure: Exploded view of over-ear headphones: ear cushion, driver, Bluetooth board, battery and touch cover

discover.title:
Follow one name
to find more.
discover.body: From a composer's name to every song credited to it, from an M3 to the albums that came out there, from an anime to its whole soundtrack.
discover.figure: Exploded view of a turntable: record, slipmat, platter, belt, tonearm and plinth

community.title: Filled in by everyone.
community.body: Once signed in, anyone can add new albums and fix mistakes, and every change is kept in the history. The data is shared under CC BY-SA 4.0 and is free to use.

paste.title: Paste a tracklist
paste.hint: One track per line. Numbers such as “01.”, “1-03” or “A1” and durations such as “3:45” are recognized; a line “Disc 2” starts a new disc.
paste.mode_update: Update tracks with the same number, add the rest

paste_credits.title: Paste credits
paste_credits.hint: Paste a whole credit list from the booklet or a shop page, one role per line, like “Composer & Arranger: Minato (M1–M3), Yuki (M4)”. Track numbers in brackets are the tracks someone worked on; without them it is the whole album. The lines under “01. Title” are that track’s, up to a blank line, and numbers after “Disc 2” are on disc 2.

paste_credits.skipped: Line {lines} wasn’t understood and won’t be added
paste_credits.unsettled: Yellow rows aren’t settled and won’t be added
